text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import datetime,json,hashlib
p=Path('mhd_llm/codex/external_model/cme_nov23')
report='''Author: Codex-external_model
Independent primary-source audit: Nov23 2025 CMEs and possible Dec3--4 comet relevance
Prepared: 2026-10-16 UTC / 2026-10-17 Europe/London

Conclusion
Both omitted DONKI cones point toward 3I/ATLAS and could affect the observation epoch under slow-wind/strong-drag or sufficiently extended-body scenarios. This is a plausible conditional effect, not evidence that the comet was inside either ICME during PN exposure. The current WSA launch-axis speeds are closer to400--425km/s, for which the modeled leading edges generally precede the PN epoch. Ambient-only modeling must therefore be presented as a baseline with transient sensitivity, and the requested CCMC run's <=1.03percent included-CME/ambient difference cannot exclude these omitted events.

Direct primary confirmation and provenance
The old kauai/webtools hosts and NASA DEMO_KEY endpoint failed. An independent search found the official CCMC September2026 migration notice, effective2026-09-30, documenting replacement hosts. Actual HTTP200 JSON was then downloaded directly from:
https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI-API/get/CME?startDate=2025-11-23&endDate=2025-11-24
https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI-API/get/CMEAnalysis?startDate=2025-11-23&endDate=2025-11-24&mostAccurateOnly=true&speed=0&halfAngle=0
https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI-API/get/IPS?startDate=2025-11-26&endDate=2025-11-27
Migration notice: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/news/major-updates/
Full immutable response bodies and SHA256/download metadata are donki_cme.json, donki_cme_analysis.json, donki_ips.json and migrated_api_provenance.json. Earlier browser exact-ID searches corroborated the entries; direct raw API is the stronger source. No sibling's numerical results or implementation were copied.

Fast event: 2025-11-23T23:30:00-CME-001
Primary LE fit865km/s, HEEQlon+90deg,lat-23deg, halfwidth21deg, time21.5Rs2025-11-24T03:06Z. Data level0, SWPC_CAT, GOES CCOR-1 running difference; speed measured at11Rs. Its note reports a faint SW CME overlapping the brighter western event, with source approximatelyS20W90, small filament eruption from22:34Z, and SUVI/STEREO-EUVI source signatures. LASCO and STEREO-A coronagraph real-time gaps limit independent geometry. Individual analysis: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/CMEAnalysis/42964/-1
Event: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/CME/42963/-1

Slow event: 2025-11-23T23:45:00-CME-001
Primary LE fit429km/s, HEEQlon+80deg,lat-8deg, halfwidth30deg, time21.5Rs2025-11-24T07:13Z. Data level0, SWPC_CAT, best fit using LASCO C2/C3 and CCOR-1 with approximate source location; not clearly seen in STA COR2. Source note describes the brighter western diffuse-front CME, filament approximatelyS20W80 at22:36Z and opening fields/arcades/dimming. The separate non-primary plane-of-sky fit363km/s has no longitude and cannot replace the deprojected fit directly.
Analysis: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/CMEAnalysis/42973/-1
Event: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/CME/42966/-1
These are leading-edge fits, not measured interplanetary shock speeds, masses, radial durations, density or magnetic flux-rope properties. No formal uncertainty intervals are supplied.

Independent in-situ context
Both primary CME records link the same IPS at STEREO-A2025-11-26T18:48Z, instruments IMPACT and PLASTIC. The separate IPS raw record reciprocally lists both. This supports a real outward disturbance but does not uniquely attribute that shock to either event or measure the comet's plasma. The contemporaneous individual ENLIL outputs predicted STA glancing arrivalsNov26 22:00 fast andNov27 00:00 slow. These are operational model predictions, not new local observations at the comet.
IPS: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/IPS/43149/-1
Fast model: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/WSA-ENLIL/42968/-1
Slow model: https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/view/WSA-ENLIL/42977/-1

Independent moving-target geometry
Use Sun-centered geometric Horizons comet/Earth states from observations ephemerides, in their common fixed inertial solar-equatorial basis. At the21.5Rs epoch, set fixed inertial axis longitude equal to Earth projected longitude plus DONKI HEEQ longitude. Do not keep HEEQ longitude fixed during propagation, because its Earth reference evolves. This gives axes76.069882214deg and66.242093432deg in the supplied inertial basis. Comet radius grows1.6557AU onNov24 12Z to1.8618AU onDec3 12Z and1.8868AU onDec4 12Z. Angular separations fast/slow are17.56/14.25deg onNov24,16.80/10.02deg onNov28,17.16/5.38deg onDec3 and17.36/4.54deg onDec4. Both remain inside nominal fitted cones; the fast cone is only3.6--3.8deg inside its nominal edge and is sensitive to direction/width errors. Direction deflection and width uncertainty are not quantified by the catalogue. geometry.json records the calculation. Angular membership alone does not establish impact, since radial timing is essential.

Drag/shape bounds (not a fitted forecast)
Original source: Dumbovic etal2021, Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences8:639986, DOI10.3389/fspas.2021.639986; author preprinthttps://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.14292. Saved PDF and extracted text. Integrate a=-gamma(v-w)|v-w| analytically from21.5Rs, with constant w and gamma. The primary study motivates w300--600km/s and gamma0.2--2e-7km^-1. Use concentric, self-similar cone, and flattening cone front options from its Eq2,4--6; the latter two are axisymmetric spherical-angular extensions of its published2D geometry. The cone factor is [cos(alpha)+sqrt(tan(halfwidth)^2-sin(alpha)^2)]/[1+tan(halfwidth)], not the different sine-SSE formula. Solve the interception against the comet's changing radius and direction. No parameter was fitted to X-rays, comet plasma, or the IPS.

With catalogue speeds and all three geometries, the drag grid gives:
  fast: Nov27 20:48 throughDec5 11:17 UTC;
  slow: Nov29 08:47 throughDec4 00:16 UTC.
Ballistic catalogue-speed fronts arrive earlier:
  fast: Nov27 08:48--21:24;
  slow: Dec1 04:25--07:13.
Restricting w to350--500km/s yields latest fastfrontDec3 12:22 and latest slowfrontDec2 14:00. Current actual PN GTIs spanDec3 13:04:03.002--Dec4 09:56:03.002,45intervals in observations/xmm_gtis.tsv; these supersede the broader earlier event/header span. A finite body or interaction can extend past a leading-edge time.

Concrete overlap examples at nominal catalogue speed:
  Slow,w300,gamma1e-7: self-similar frontDec3 15:04:48; flattening frontDec3 13:18:07. Both are within actual PN GTIs.
  Slow,w300,gamma2e-7: fronts cluster lateDec3/earlyDec4.
  Fast self-similar,w300,gamma1e-7 arrivesDec4 15:53, outside current PN GTIs but inside manuscript pointing span.
The all-case CSV records exact PN-GTI membership. A +/-20percent speed sweep is also supplied solely as sensitivity, not a measured confidence interval. Grid counts are not probabilities. Constant drag/ambient wind, no Lorentz forces, no front interactions/deflection, and extrapolated early speeds preclude precise arrival prediction. Self-similar and flattening fronts differ materially at the fast flank; present their difference as geometry uncertainty.

Actual ambient-map diagnostic
At launch time and direction, supplied WSA inner-boundary speeds are397.30km/s fast and424.78km/s slow. Across the cone footprints,16/50/84percentiles are312/374/414 and339/404/469km/s. Thus w300 late-arrival cases are slow-wind sensitivities rather than central launch conditions. Those source values do not measure the effective drag wind over the entire moving path, which evolves and can include stream interactions. ambient_launch_speed_diagnostic.json preserves this independent map sample. For w400 with gamma2e-7, self-similar fast/slow fronts arriveDec2 04:11/Dec1 14:38; extrapolating these alone would favor earlier passage. We cannot infer precise PN-period density enhancement from the current evidence.

Concrete inexpensive MHD sensitivity inputs
cme_boundary_nominal.csv and cme_boundary_long.csv are two-row inputs with exact requested schema, Nov1 MJD60980 origin, start at each primary time21.5Rs, fixed inertial axes, measured widths and leading-edge speeds. Nominal duration0.5day and long duration1day, densityfactor4 and temperaturefactor1 are explicit scenario assumptions. They are not catalogue measurements or a universal standard. The narrow-shell radial-thickness proxies from the cone geometry are2.66h and7.09h; these proxies themselves are not measured boundary-crossing durations.12/24h cases deliberately test a broader extended-body response. Their leading front is a simple hydro cone, not a unique geometrical reconstruction of the coronal image or a magnetic flux rope.

Requested taper/overlap semantics are recorded in boundary_scenario_provenance.json: flat angular core to0.9halfwidth,cos^2edge;10percent temporal sin^2ramps; choose greatest space-time weight, later row on a tie, rather than multiplying overlapping density enhancements. Given near-simultaneous launches and overlapping inferred volumes, such overlap handling avoids inventing a densityfactor16. It remains a conditional numerical closure for possibly interacting ejecta, not a mass-conserving reconstruction of two independent measured structures. A densityfactor4 at Tfactor1 increases thermal pressure by4; its effect must be reported as a scenario. Preserve actual ambient speed/density/temperature map between pulses. Avoid applying the ambient n~v^-2 calibration to the imposed fast cone; this would suppress its density precisely when the hydro-CME test intends an enhancement. Recompute the tangential ideal-induction boundary consistently when changing speed. Do not perturb Br into a fabricated flux rope.

Interpretation and remaining limits
Run the same mesh and geometry with ambient/nominal/long inputs and compare time series and GTI-weighted proton flux. Large differences would establish sensitivity, not identify the correct case. Small differences would constrain only these selected speed/width/density/duration scenarios; they would not exclude magnetic ejecta, other catalogue uncertainties or evolving coronal structure. Independent published plasma/field signatures at STA can support context, but the two linked events and broad separation prevent using the IPS as unique event calibration. Neither cone has a direct local comet solar-wind observation. Report the requested CCMC comparison as one conditional external-model benchmark and retain input uncertainty separately from numerical convergence.
'''
(p/'report.txt').write_text(report)
now=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc);note=Path('mhd_llm/shared_notes')/f'codex_external_model_{now.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%MZ")}_nov23_cme_correction.txt'

No magnetic flux rope or exact CME prediction is claimed.\n\nOwn external_model/report.txt updated to supersede the ambient-omission inference. No main solver edits or large simulation runs performed.\n')
print(p/'report.txt');print(note)
